name: Pili torti

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and microscopic hair shaft analysis criteria

criteria.description: Presence of hair shafts twisted 180 degrees along their axis observed under light microscopy
Hair fragility with easy breakage and sparse scalp hair
Presence of associated systemic features in syndromic forms (e.g., sensorineural hearing loss, nail dystrophy)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Identification of characteristic twisted hair shafts on microscopy plus clinical evidence of fragile, sparse hair
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by microscopic hair shaft examination; genetic testing may be used in syndromic cases.

searchTerms: hair that is coarse or fine

laboratory: Light microscopy showing hair shafts twisted 180 degrees
Trichoscopy revealing flattened and twisted hair shafts
imaging: Audiometry confirming sensorineural hearing loss in syndromic cases
genetic: Mutations in genes such as BCS1L, ATP6V0A2, or others depending on syndromic association
other: Clinical examination revealing brittle, sparse hair and nail abnormalities

distinguishingFeatures: Beaded hair appearance on microscopy instead of twisted shafts
Nodes and fractures along hair shaft rather than uniform twisting
Hair breakage due to mechanical trauma

redFlags: Rapid progression of hair loss with systemic symptoms
Signs of multisystem involvement suggesting syndromic form
references: Hair shaft disorders: clinical and microscopic features, Dermatol Clin. 2013
Genetic basis of pili torti and associated syndromes, J Med Genet. 2018
